title: Milo's Cafe: a neighborhood café with a patio that follows the sky
tag: Café website, Morrisville, NC · Launching Nov 2026
summaryLead: A one-page site for a Morrisville café. Menu, prices, patio, and a way to order.
story: Milo's is a European-style café in Morrisville, run by Menad and Liliana Haliche. When people look it up they want three things: what's on the menu, what it costs, and whether the patio's worth it today. The new site answers all three. At the top is an illustrated patio that follows the real weather and time of day. The menu is on the page instead of a PDF, and every drink has a little glass that pours when you tap it. Ordering is one tap. It's porcelain, cobalt and one gold, with the gold saved for the order button.

Show whether the patio's worth it today.

features.title: A hero that says what it is
features.text: A short headline, two buttons, and the patio right underneath.
features.alt: Milo's Cafe home page with the patio scene
features.story: Headlines are Fraunces and body text is Instrument Sans. Sizes step up on a major-third scale from 17px.

features.title: The patio, drawn live
features.text: The sun, clouds, rain and wind follow the real sky over Morrisville. A slider scrubs through the day.
features.alt: Milo's patio scene in the morning
features.story: A photo can't tell you if today's a patio day. This can. The line work is hand-drawn with a slight wobble, the trees sway, and the umbrellas close at night. If the weather feed drops, you get a plain daytime sky.

features.title: Drinks that pour
features.text: Every drink has a small glass beside its price. Hover or tap it and the layers pour in, with a line saying what's in it.
features.alt: Milo's drinks menu with the Americano glass open
features.story: Nobody knows what a cortado is until they see one. The glass fills layer by layer, in the order the drink is built, and steam drifts off the top. Under it, a line like "1 part espresso, 2 parts hot water". Each drink has its own colors, from espresso to matcha. It's a small SVG with CSS, so it stays quiet until someone asks.

features.title: Their story, up front
features.text: Who opened it, what they serve and the sandwich-shop award, next to a photo of the front door. Below it, a Pair it picker for first-timers.
features.story: First-timers hit a long menu and don't know where to start. Pair it picks from lists we wrote by hand. No account, no tracking.

features.title: A menu you can search
features.text: Food and drinks, a meat-free filter, jump links, and a star on guest favorites.
features.alt: Milo's menu with Food and Drinks tabs
features.story: Menus usually sit in a PDF nobody can search. Here every dish is its own entry, so a new seasonal drink is one line to add.

features.title: Prices on the page
features.text: Toast, salads, focaccia and crepes, each with a short description and a price.
features.story: Dotted lines run from each dish to its price, like a printed menu. The cups beside the drinks stay still until you hover, then they pour.

features.title: Inside and out
features.text: The gravel patio, the green wall and the bench room, so you know what you're walking into.

features.title: Reviews in their own words
features.text: The rating, one pulled quote and short lines from guests.

features.title: Instagram and the room
features.text: Photos pulled from their own Instagram.

features.title: On a phone
features.text: Order and Call stay pinned to the bottom of the screen.
